title: Epistulae
author: Cyprian
source: Translated by Claude from stoa0104a.stoa012.opp-lat1, as held by Open Greek and Latin's CSEL.
statement: An AI-generated translation. No specialist has reviewed it.
availability: CC BY-SA 4.0, as its source requires: credit Open Greek and Latin's CSEL and this AI translation, and share adaptations under the same licence.

passages.original: Qoapropter cum, sicut scribitis, fratres dilectissimi, et ut Felix et Sabinus collegae nostri adseuerant utque alius Felix de Caesaraugusta fidei cultor ac defensor ueritatis litteris suis significat, Basilides et Martialis nefando idololatriae libello contaminati sint, Basilides adhuc insuper praeter libelli maculam cum infirmitate decumberet, in Deum blasphemauerit et se blasphemasse confessus sit et episcopatum pro conscientiae suae uulnere sponte deponens ad agendam paenitentiam conuersus sit Deum deprecans et satis gratulans si sibi uel laico communicare contingeret, Martialis quoque praeter gentilium turpia et lutulenta conuiuia in collegio diu frequentata et filios in eodem collegio exterarum gentium more apud profana sepulcra depositos et alienigenis consepultos, actis etiam publice habitis apud procuratorem ducenarium obtemperasse se idololatriae et Christum negasse contestatus sit cumque alia multa sint et grauia delicta quibus Basilides et Martialis inplicati tenentur: frustra tales episcopatum sibi usurpare conantur, cum manifestius sit eiusmodi homines nec ecclesiae Christi posse praeesse nec Deo sacrificia offerre debere, maxime cum iam pridem nobiscum et cum omnibus omnino episcopis in toto mundo constitutis etiam Cornelius collega noster, sacerdos pacificus ac iustus et martyrio quoque dignatione Domini honoratus, decreuerit eiusmodi homines ad paenitentiam quidem agendam posse admitti, ab ordinatione autem cleri adque sacerdotali honore prohiberi.
passages.english: Therefore, dearest brothers, since, as you write, and as our colleagues Felix and Sabinus assert, and as another Felix, of Caesaraugusta, a cultivator of the faith and defender of the truth, indicates in his letter, Basilides and Martialis have been defiled by the abominable certificate of idolatry; [since] Basilides, moreover, besides the stain of the certificate, when he lay sick in bed, blasphemed against God, and confessed that he had blasphemed, and, laying down his episcopate of his own accord because of the wound of his conscience, turned to doing penance, entreating God and being well content if it should fall to him to be admitted to communion even as a layman; [since] Martialis too, besides long frequenting the shameful and filthy banquets of the gentiles in a guild, and placing his sons in that same guild, after the custom of foreign nations, at profane tombs and burying them with strangers, also declared in official proceedings held publicly before a ducenarian procurator that he had complied with idolatry and denied Christ; and since there are many other grave offences in which Basilides and Martialis are held entangled: such men try in vain to usurp the episcopate for themselves, since it is quite plain that men of this kind can neither preside over the church of Christ nor ought to offer sacrifices to God, especially since long ago, together with us and with absolutely all the bishops established throughout the whole world, our colleague Cornelius too, a peaceable and just bishop, and honoured also with martyrdom by the Lord's favour, decreed that men of this kind may indeed be admitted to do penance, but are to be barred from ordination to the clergy and from priestly honour.
passages.notes: 'Qoapropter' read as 'Quapropter' (scanning error). 'libellus' is the certificate of having sacrificed issued during the Decian persecution. 'procurator ducenarius' is a procurator of the 200,000-sesterces salary grade. 'sacerdos' here refers to a bishop.

passages.original: Porro autem quod quidam eos salutari aqua et fide legitima Christi gratiam consecutos non christianos sed clinicos uocant, non inuenio unde hoc nomen adsumant: nisi forte qui plura et secretiora legerunt, apud Hippocratem uel Soranum clinicos istos deprehenderunt. ego enim qui clinicum de euangelio noui scio paralytico illi et debili per longa aetatis curricula in lecto iacenti nihil infirmitatem suam obfuisse quo minus ad firmitatem caelestem plenissime perueniret, nec tantum indulgentia dominica excitatum de grabato esse, sed ipsum grabatum suum reparatis et uegetatis uiribus sustulisse.
passages.english: Furthermore, as to the fact that some call those who have obtained the grace of Christ by the saving water and lawful faith not Christians but 'clinics', I cannot find where they take this name from, unless perhaps those who have read more and more recondite works have found these 'clinics' in Hippocrates or Soranus. For I, who know of a 'clinic' from the Gospel, know that for that paralytic, infirm and lying in bed through the long course of his life, his infirmity was no hindrance at all to his attaining heavenly strength most fully; and not only was he raised from his pallet by the Lord's mercy, but with his strength restored and invigorated he himself took up his pallet.
passages.notes: 'Clinici' (from Greek klinē, 'bed') denotes those baptized on their sickbed; Cyprian puns on its medical sense (bedridden patients in medical writers).

passages.original: eundem nouit filium Christum de uirgine Maria natum, qui sermo caro factus sit, qui peccata nostra portauerit, qui mortem moriendo uicerit, qui resurrectionem carnis per semet ipsum primus initiauerit et discipulis suis quod in eadem carne resurrexisset ostenderit? longe alia est apud Marcionem sed et apud ceteros haereticos fides. immo nihil est apud illos nisi perfidia et blasphemia et contentio sanitatis et ueritatis inimica. quomodo ergo potest uideri qui apud illos baptizatur consecutus esse peccatorum remissam et diuinae indulgentiae gratiam per suam fidem qui ipsius fidei non habuerit ueritatem?
passages.english: Does he acknowledge the same Son, Christ, born of the Virgin Mary, who as the Word was made flesh, who bore our sins, who conquered death by dying, who first by his own self began the resurrection of the flesh and showed his disciples that he had risen in that same flesh? Far different is the faith among Marcion and also among the other heretics. Rather, there is nothing among them but faithlessness and blasphemy and contentiousness, hostile to soundness and truth. How then can one who is baptized among them seem to have obtained the remission of sins and the grace of divine pardon through his faith, when he did not have the truth of the faith itself?
passages.notes: "remissam" is evidently a scanning error for "remissam" > "remissionem"; translated as "remission".

passages.original: ut habere quis possit Deum patrem, habeat ante ecclesiam matrem. cum uero nulla omnino haeresis, sed neque aliquod schisma habere salutaris baptismi sanctificationem foris possit, in tantum Stephani fratris nostri obstinatio dura prorupit, ut etiam de Marcionis baptismo, item Valentini et Appelletis et ceterorum blasphemantium in Deum patrem contendat filios Deo nasci, et illic in nomine Iesu Christi dicat remissionem peccatorum dari ubi blasphematur in patrem et Dominum Deum Christum.
passages.english: so that whoever would have God as Father must first have the Church as mother. But although no heresy at all, nor indeed any schism, can have the sanctification of saving baptism outside, the hard obstinacy of our brother Stephen has broken out to such an extent that he contends that sons are born to God even from the baptism of Marcion, and likewise of Valentinus and Apelles and the rest who blaspheme against God the Father, and says that remission of sins is given there in the name of Jesus Christ where blasphemy is uttered against the Father and against the Lord God Christ.
passages.notes: The passage begins mid-sentence ("ut habere..."); the preceding clause is not included. "Appelletis" taken as Apelles, the disciple of Marcion.
